ai-opportunity-audit: Choose one task you can measure.
List three recurring tasks, pick one with approved inputs and a reviewable output, and record a baseline before testing.

Illustrative example: drafting internal meeting summaries. A person checked actions and owners. The draft was quicker, but missed an owner; the team chose Revise and added an owner check. No measured client result is claimed.
Turn the uncertainty into a testable decision.
product-decision-canvas: Write one assumption and its decision rule.
Pick a user decision, write what you believe will help, and define evidence that would make you continue, revise or stop.

Illustrative example: a paper onboarding prototype. Participants misunderstood the first instruction, so the designer revised the wording rather than declaring the idea validated. This does not establish market demand.
Turn a tested method into a repeatable workflow.
ai-workflow-starter-kit: Define one workflow and three tests.
Write the input, approved context, output format and human review criteria. Choose three varied, non-sensitive inputs.

Illustrative example: grouping synthetic interview notes. Two inputs produced supported themes; one invented a quote. The practitioner chose Stop for automatic sharing and retained human review. This is not a model benchmark.
Assess where a reliable workflow could create useful value.
design-thinking-workshop: Observe one everyday task and separate three observations from interpretations.
Observe one everyday task and separate three observations from interpretations.
Illustrative workshop example: a student observes confusion at a library returns desk. They test a paper sign and a revised service handoff before proposing an app.

concept-design-workshop: Write three concepts that differ in mechanism, not just styling.
Write three concepts that differ in mechanism, not just styling.
Illustrative workshop example: three ways to improve a public waiting experience use seating information, an assisted queue and a physical token. The team tests the uncertainty behind each direction.
